Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.5.
Upādinnattika (The Triplet on Clung-to)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of the root condition—[namely,] a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging.
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates arise … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise;

at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one acquired and subject-to-clinging aggregate, three aggregates and the matter produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa) arise … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and the matter produced by kamma arise;
dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis arises; dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise.

Dependent on one great primary element that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arise three great primary elements … dependent on two great primary elements, there arise two great primary elements;
dependent on the great primary elements, there arises derived matter consisting of kamma-produced matter.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of root condition: dependent on the aggregates that are both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arises mind-originated matter.

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, there arise states that are both acquired and subject to clinging, as well as states that are not acquired but are subject to clinging, by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*):
dependent on one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter; ...
[and so on] ... dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on one great primary element that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging …pe….
Three great elements … [and so on] … dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter is derived matter.
Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging, a state that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and is not subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging, by way of root condition: dependent on the aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and are not subject to clinging, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and is not subject to clinging, there arise states that are both not acquired by clinging but subject to clinging and not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging, by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not acquired by clinging and is not subject to clinging, [the other] three...
The aggregates and mind-produced matter ... [and so on] ... dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.

Dependent on states that are not acquired by clinging but are subject to clinging, and states that are neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging, by way of root condition—dependent on aggregates that are neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging and the great elements.
Mind-produced matter.

Dependent on states that are both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, and states that are not acquired through clinging but are subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not acquired through clinging but is subject to clinging by way of root condition: mind-produced matter dependent on the aggregates that are acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, and the great primary elements.
Object condition.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of object condition: dependent on one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging … pe ….
Dependent on a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging … pe … by way of object condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging arises by way of the predominance condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … [dependent on] one great primary element.
Dependent on [the four] great elements … dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter is derived matter.
Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging … three [answers].

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging but conducive to clinging and a state that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging, [arises] a state that is not acquired by clinging but conducive to clinging … [and so forth].
A state arises by way of predominance condition: mind-produced matter dependent upon aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging and the great elements.
[The same applies for] immediate and so forth.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of proximity condition … by way of contiguity condition … by way of co-nascence condition:

dependent on one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging … and so on … at the moment of rebirth-linking … and so on … dependent on one great primary … and so on … dependent on the great primaries, [arises] kamma-produced form.
Derived form; dependent on one great primary element of non-percipient beings … pe … dependent on great primary elements, derived form consisting of kamma-result.
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging … three.

Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of conascence condition—a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging … [and so forth].

In dependence on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter …pe… in dependence on one great primary element …pe… in dependence on the great primary elements, there arises mind-produced derived matter. External … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced:
in dependence on one great primary element …pe….
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to and not subject to clinging … three.

Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging and a state that is not clung-to and not subject to clinging … [and so on] … dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging … [and so on] … Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging and a state that is not clung-to and not subject to clinging, [arises] a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging … [and so on].
Reciprocity Condition:
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of reciprocity condition—
dependent on one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging.
Three aggregates and the [heart-]base … dependent on the aggregates, the base arises; dependent on the base, the aggregates arise;
dependent on one great primary element … dependent on two great primary elements, two great primary elements arise; one great primary element of non-percipient beings … [and so on].
Dependent on a state that is not acquired but is subject to clinging … external … nutriment-originated … temperature-originated … [and so on].
Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging … [and so on] … By way of dependence condition (*nissaya-paccaya*):
Dependent on a state that is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging, there are nine [answers]. By way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*): three [answers].
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of prenascence condition … three.
Repetition (āsevana).
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging arises by way of repetition-condition:

dependent on one aggregate that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging … pe … Dependent on a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging, a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging arises by way of repetition-condition: dependent on one aggregate that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging … pe … Kamma.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of kamma-condition. (Nine [phases] are the same as under the root-condition.
Resultant:
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of resultant-condition... three.

Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging arises by way of resultant condition: dependent on one great primary element … [and so on] … dependent on the great primary elements, mind-originated derived matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging, a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging arises by way of resultant condition: dependent on one resultant aggregate that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … nine.
Food, etc.
Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging,

there arises a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging by way of nutriment-condition … pe … faculty-condition … jhāna-condition … path-condition … association-condition … dissociation-condition … presence-condition … absence-condition … disappearance-condition … non-disappearance-condition.
(Just as the section on dependence (*paṭiccavāra*) of the wholesome triad (*kusalattika*) has been explained in detail by way of recitation, so too should it be explained here.
The Chapter on Enumeration (*saṅkhyāvāra*),
Pure (*suddha*).

In the case of the root condition (hetu), there are nine; in the object condition (ārammaṇa), three; in the predominance condition (adhipati), five; in the proximity condition (anantara), three; in the contiguity condition (samanantara), three;

in the co-nascence condition (sahajāta), nine; in the mutuality condition (aññamañña), three; in the support condition (nissaya), nine; in the decisive support condition (upanissaya), three; in the prenascence condition (purejāta), three; in the repetition condition (āsevana), two;

in the kamma condition (kamma), nine; in the resultant condition (vipāka), nine; in the nutriment condition (āhāra), nine; in the faculty condition (indriya), nine; in the jhāna condition (jhāna), nine; in the path condition (magga), nine; in the association condition (sampayutta) [there are nine].
Three [in the case of] dissociation, nine in presence, three in absence, three in disappearance, and nine in non-disappearance.
In the *Hetuduka* (Root-Duad):
with the root-condition as the cause, there are three in the object-condition …pe… and nine in non-disappearance.
(Just as the enumeration of the "dependent" [paṭicca] in the *Kusalattika* was counted by way of the path of recitation, so too should it be counted here.
Positive Order (*Anuloma*).
1.5.1.2. Negative Order of Conditions (*Paccayapaccanīya*).
Section on Analysis:

Not-root Condition. Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of the not-root condition: [that is,] a rootless [state].
Dependent on one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging, there arise three aggregates; dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates.

At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging, there arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter …pe… dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and kamma-produced matter; dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base.
Dependent on a base, the aggregates [arise]; dependent on one great primary element, three great primary elements [arise] ...

pe ... dependent on the great primary elements, kamma-born derived matter arises; in the case of non-percipient beings, dependent on one great primary element ... pe ... dependent on the great primary elements, kamma-born derived matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*), a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging arises by way of the non-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*): dependent on rootless aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging, mind-originated matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, states that are both acquired and subject to clinging, as well as states that are not acquired but subject to clinging, arise by way of the non-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging, three aggregates [arise].
And mind-originated matter …pe… dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-originated matter.
Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging, a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging arises by way of the root-condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging, there arise three aggregates and mind-originated matter …pe…
Dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-originated matter.
One great primary element that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging … dependent on the great primaries, there arises mind-originated derived matter.

One external great primary element … one nutriment-originated great primary element … one temperature-originated great primary element … dependent on the great primaries, there arises derived matter. Dependent on [the great primaries] associated with doubt …
In dependence on aggregates accompanied by restlessness, arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.

In dependence on states that are both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, and states that are not acquired through clinging but are subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not acquired through clinging but is subject to clinging, by way of the non-root condition (*na-hetu-paccaya*):
in dependence on rootless aggregates that are acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, and on the great elements (*mahābhūta*).
Matter produced by mind.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of the condition of non-object: at the moment of rebirth-linking.
Dependent on aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging, there arises derived matter; dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;
dependent on one great primary element … pe … dependent on one great primary element of non-percipient beings … pe ….

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging arises by way of the condition of non-object: dependent on aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging, mind-originated matter arises.
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of the condition of not-object:

dependent on aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging, mind-originated matter [arises]; dependent on one great primary element … and so on … external … nutriment-originated … dependent on one great primary element of temperature-originated matter … and so on …

Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to and not-object-of-clinging, a state that is not-clung-to but is an object-of-clinging arises by way of the condition of non-object: dependent on the aggregates that are not-clung-to and not-objects-of-clinging, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is both not-clung-to but an object-of-clinging and not-clung-to and not-an-object-of-clinging, a state that is not-clung-to but an object-of-clinging arises by way of the condition of non-object: dependent on the aggregates that are not-clung-to and not-objects-of-clinging and the great elements.
Dependent on mind-originated matter.

Dependent on states that are both clung-to and subject to clinging, and states that are not clung-to but subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of the object condition:
dependent on aggregates that are both clung-to and subject to clinging, and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is not dominant, acquired, and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not dominant, acquired, and subject to clinging, by way of the non-dominant condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*)—[conception is complete]—three [answers].
Dependent on a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging... one [answer].

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging, a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging arises by way of the non-predominance condition: dependent on aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging, there arises a predominance that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging.

Dependent on a state that is both acquired by clinging and subject to clinging, and a state that is not acquired by clinging and subject to clinging, a state that is not acquired by clinging and subject to clinging arises by way of the non-predominance condition:
dependent on aggregates that are acquired by clinging and subject to clinging, and the great elements, there arises mind-originated matter.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of non-immediate condition … [and so on] … by way of non-samanantara condition … by way of non-mutuality condition … by way of non-strong-dependence condition … by way of non-prenascence condition.

… not by way of postnascence condition … not by way of repetition condition … [and so on] … Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging arises by way of repetition condition: dependent on one resultant aggregate that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging, three aggregates [arise]. (Abbreviated.
Not-kamma.
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of not-kamma-condition:

dependent on aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging, there arises volition that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging. Dependent on an external [great primary]… dependent on nutriment-originated… dependent on one temperature-originated great primary… (and so forth).

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging, a state that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging arises by way of the non-kamma condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging, volition that is not acquired by clinging and not conducive to clinging arises.

[Dependent on] a state that is acquired by clinging and conducive to clinging, a state that is acquired by clinging and conducive to clinging arises by way of the non-resultant condition: dependent on one great primary of non-percipient beings … pe … dependent on the great primaries, kamma-born matter and derived matter arise.

Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to but subject to clinging (*anupādinnupādāniya*), a state that is not-clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of non-resultant condition (*navipākapaccaya*) … one.

Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging (*anupādinnaanupādāniya*), a state that is neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging arises by way of non-resultant condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate that is neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging, three aggregates [arise] … three.
Dependent on a state that is both not-clung-to but subject to clinging and neither-clung-to nor subject to clinging, a state that is not-clung-to but subject to clinging [arises] … one.

A state arises by way of non-resultant condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates that are neither clung-to nor conducive to clinging and the great primary elements, mind-produced matter arises. [Not-nutriment condition...]
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of non-nutriment condition:

dependent on one great primary element of non-percipient beings … pe … Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of non-nutriment condition: external … dependent on one great primary element born of temperature … pe … Not by way of faculty condition.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of non-faculty condition: dependent on the great elements of non-percipient beings, the material life-faculty arises.

Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of non-faculty condition: external [matter] … nutriment-produced matter … dependent on one temperature-produced great element … (and so forth).
[Non-jhāna]
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of the not-jhāna condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness, three aggregates arise …pe… dependent on one great primary of non-percipient beings …pe….

Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of the not-jhāna condition: dependent on an external [great primary] … dependent on a nutriment-originated great primary … dependent on a temperature-originated great primary …pe….

Dependent on a state that is both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, a state that is both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging arises by way of not-path condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate that is both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, three aggregates [arise] … five.
Not-association.

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*), a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging arises by way of non-association condition (*na-sampayutta-paccaya*). (This is the same as the non-object condition.
Non-dissociation:
Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging arises by way of non-dissociation condition—in the formless realm (*arūpa*).
Dependent on one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, three aggregates [arise] …pe… dependent on one great primary element of non-percipient beings …pe….
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging arises by way of non-dissociation condition:
in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, three aggregates [arise] …pe… external … nutriment-produced … [and so forth].
… dependent on one great primary element originating from temperature … [and so forth] … Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging,
a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane,
dependent on one aggregate that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging, three aggregates [arise] … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates [arise].

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises by way of the non-absence condition … by way of the non-disappearance condition.
(As the negative section was expanded in the Faultless Triplet, so it should be expanded here.)
In the Enumeration Chapter,
regarding the pure [conditioning], there are five for not-root, six for not-object, six for not-predominance, six for not-proximity, and six for not-contiguity.
Six with mutuality, six with strong-dependence, seven with prenascence, nine with postnascence, nine with repetition,
two with kamma, six with resultant, two with nutriment, two with faculty,
two with jhāna, five with path, six with association, three with dissociation, six with absence, and six with disappearance.
1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
The Non-root Pair (Nahetuduka)
With not-root condition and not-object condition, there are four; with not-predominance, five; with not-proximity, four ...
pe ... with not-repetition, five; with not-kamma, one; with not-resultant, two ... pe ... with not-jhāna, two; with not-path, five;
with not-association, four; with not-dissociation, two ... pe ... with not-disappearance, four.
It should be counted in the same way as the counting in the *Kusalattika*.

Hetu-duka: With root condition, there are six [instances] for non-object; ... seven for non-prenascence; nine for non-postnascence; nine for non-repetition; two for non-kamma; six for non-resultant; six for non-association; three for non-dissociation; ... six for non-disappearance.
(The count should be made in the same way as the positive-negative enumeration in the Wholesome Triplet.)

Not-root Pair (Nahetuduka).

With not-root condition, there are two [answers] for object ... pe ... five for conascence, two for mutuality, five for dependence, two for strong-dependence, two for prenascence, one for repetition, five for kamma ...
pe ... five for jhāna, one for path, two for association, five for dissociation ... pe ... five for non-disappearance.

1.5.2. Chapter on Co-nascence (Sahajātavāra) 1.5.2.1–4.

Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka) A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging arises together with a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of the root condition (hetupaccaya).
The section on dependence (paṭiccavāra) is similar to the section on co-nascence (sahajātavāra).
Section on Co-nascence. 1.5.3.
Section on Conditions (paccayavāra).
1.5.3.1. Analysis of the Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma Vibhaṅgavāra): Root Condition (Hetu)
Conditioned by a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, by way of root condition:

conditioned by one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on] … conditioned by the aggregates, the physical basis arises;
conditioned by the physical basis, the aggregates arise; conditioned by one great primary element, three great primary elements arise … [and so on] … conditioned by the great primary elements …
Kamma-produced matter is derived matter; conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise aggregates that are both clung-to and objects of clinging.
Conditioned by a state that is both clung-to and an object of clinging, a state that is not clung-to but is an object of clinging arises by way of root condition:

conditioned by aggregates that are both clung-to and objects of clinging, mind-originated matter arises; conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise aggregates that are not clung-to but are objects of clinging.

Conditioned by a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*), a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging (*anupādinnaanupādāniya*) arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*): conditioned by the [heart-]base, the aggregates that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging arise.

Conditioned by a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, states that are both acquired and subject to clinging, as well as states that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging, arise by way of root-condition:
conditioned by one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … .
Conditioned by a state that is not-clung-to but subject-to-clinging, a state that is not-clung-to but subject-to-clinging arises by way of root-condition … one.
Conditioned by a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subject-to-clinging, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subject-to-clinging arises by way of root-condition … three.

Conditioned by a state that is both clung-to and subject-to-clinging and a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subject-to-clinging, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subject-to-clinging [arises]… [one].

A state arises by way of root-condition: conditioned by one aggregate that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise …pe… conditioned by two aggregates and the base, two aggregates arise.
Conditioned by a state that is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging and a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging, a state that is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging [arises].
A state arises by way of root-condition: mind-produced matter arises conditioned by aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging and the great elements.
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging arises conditioned by a state that is both clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging and a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging.
Arising by way of root condition: conditioned by acquired-and-object-of-clinging aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises;
conditioned by one non-acquired-but-object-of-clinging aggregate and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise …pe… conditioned by two aggregates and the [heart-]base, two aggregates arise.
