Lust arises; wrong view arises. Co-nascent predominance: unclung-to but subject-to-clinging predominance is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A state that is neither clung-to nor subject-to-clinging is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that is neither clung-to nor subject-to-clinging.
Condition: object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the path and the fruit by way of predominance-condition.
Conascence-predominance: a predominance that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance-condition.
A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Noble ones, having emerged from the Path, esteem and review the Path;
they esteem and review the Fruit; they esteem and review Nibbāna. Nibbāna...
It is a condition for the state of lineage (*gotrabhū*) and for purification (*vodāna*) by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). As co-nascent predominance:
a predominance that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for mind-produced matter by way of predominance-condition.
A phenomenon that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is [a condition] for both that which is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging and that which is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging.
The predominance condition for the Dhamma. Co-nascent predominance:
A predominance that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Immediate...
A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*):
preceding aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for subsequent aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging by way of proximity-condition;
the fivefold sense-consciousness is a condition for the resultant mind-element by way of proximity-condition.
The resultant mind-element is a condition for the resultant mind-consciousness-element by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

A state that is acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging by way of proximity-condition: the life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) is a condition for adverting; the resultant mind-consciousness-element is a condition for the functional mind-consciousness-element by way of proximity-condition.
A state that is not acquired but subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging by way of proximity-condition: the preceding...

Preceding aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging are related to succeeding aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging by way of proximity condition (*anantarapaccaya*);

adaptation (*anuloma*) is related to change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*) ... adaptation is related to purification (*vodāna*) ... advertence (*āvajjanā*) is related to aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging by way of proximity condition.
A state that is not clung to but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung to and subject to clinging by way of proximity condition:

adverting is a condition for the five types of consciousness by way of proximity condition; aggregates that are not clung to but are subject to clinging are a condition for emergence by way of proximity condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging by way of proximity condition: change-of-lineage for the path;
purification for the path; adaptation for the attainment of fruition; for one emerging from cessation;
and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception for the attainment of fruition, by way of proximity condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and does not lead to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired by clinging and does not lead to clinging by way of proximity-condition (anantara-paccaya):

preceding aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and do not lead to clinging are a condition for subsequent aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and do not lead to clinging by way of proximity-condition.
The path is a condition for the fruit... the fruit is a condition for the fruit by way of proximity-condition.

A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for a state that is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*)—the fruit is a condition for emergence by way of proximity-condition.
Immediate (*samanantara*):

A state that is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging is a condition for a state that is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging by way of immediate-condition. (This is the same as the proximity-condition.)
A co-nascent state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of the co-nascent condition:

one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for three aggregates by way of the co-nascent condition; ... [and so on] ... two aggregates [are conditions] for two [aggregates].

Of the aggregates … [etc. … at the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a conascence condition for three aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma;
… two aggregates are conascence conditions for two aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma;

… [and so on] … the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis; … the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates; … one great primary element … [etc. … is a condition for the other great primary elements.

Three great primary elements (mahābhūta) ... [etc. ... three great primary elements are related to one great primary element ... [etc. ... two great primary elements are related to two great primary elements ... [etc. ...
the great primary elements are related to kamma-produced derived matter (upādārūpa) by way of co-nascence condition (sahajāta-paccaya).
One great primary element of non-percipient beings ... [etc. ... [is related to its corresponding derived matter].

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging: the aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging and for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging:
one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging [is a condition] for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

Material phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of co-nascence condition …pe… two aggregates are related to two aggregates and to mind-produced material phenomena by way of co-nascence condition.

A state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is related to a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of co-nascence condition— a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging...

One aggregate is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … pe … two aggregates are conditions, by way of co-nascence condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
One great primary that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging … pe … the great primaries are [conditions] for mind-produced matter.

...pe... externally ... nutriment-originated ... temperature-originated one great primary element ...pe... the great primary elements are a condition for derived matter by way of co-nascence condition.
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging by way of co-nascence condition.

Condition: One aggregate that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for three aggregates … two aggregates are a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for two aggregates.

A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state that is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging: the aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not-clung-to and not-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state that is both not-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging and for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging. One aggregate that is not-clung-to and not-liable-to-clinging is a condition,
by way of co-nascence condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … [and so on] … two aggregates.
Two aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.

States that are not acquired by clinging but are subject to clinging, and states that are neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging, are a condition for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging by way of co-nascence condition—
the aggregates that are neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging, together with the great elements, are [conditions] for mind-produced [matter].

[Material] phenomena are related to [material] phenomena by way of co-nascence condition. Both acquired-and-grasped and not-acquired-but-grasped phenomena are related to a not-acquired-but-grasped phenomenon by way of co-nascence condition:
the acquired-and-grasped aggregates and the great primaries are related to mind-originated [matter].
[Material] phenomena are related to [material] phenomena by way of co-nascence condition.
Mutuality:

A phenomenon that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a phenomenon that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of mutuality condition—a phenomenon that is both clung-to and subject to clinging...
One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of mutuality-condition …pe… two aggregates are conditions for two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking,

one aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for three aggregates and the physical basis …pe… the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis …pe… the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates …pe… one great primary element is a condition for three [great primary elements] …pe…
Of the great elements … [and so on] … two great elements are a condition for two great elements … [and so on] … one great element of non-percipient beings … [and so on].
A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition, by way of mutuality condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging:

one aggregate that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition for three aggregates … [and so on] … two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of mutuality condition.
Condition: One great primary element … [and so on] … an external [great primary element] … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced one great primary element … [and so on].
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of mutuality condition, for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging:
one aggregate that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for three aggregates … two aggregates are conditions for two aggregates … [and so on].
Supported condition:
A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of supported condition, for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging.
One aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of supported condition, for three aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe …

One great primary element …pe… one great primary element of non-percipient beings …pe… the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition, by way of support-condition (nissaya-paccaya), for the aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging.

A state that is acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of support-condition, for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging— the [physical basis] that is acquired and subject to clinging.

The aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the support-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*). The physical basis (*vatthu*) is a condition for the aggregates that are not acquired by clinging but are subject to clinging by way of the support-condition.

A state that is acquired by clinging and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging by way of the support-condition—the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates that are neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging by way of the support-condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of support-condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging.
One aggregate that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of support-condition,
for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter …pe… two aggregates are conditions, by way of support-condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
[Material] form is a condition for [material] forms by way of the support-condition (nissaya-paccaya).
A state that is not-clung-to-but-susceptible-to-clinging is a condition for a state that is not-clung-to-but-susceptible-to-clinging ... one [way].
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-susceptible-to-clinging ... three [ways].

States that are both acquired and subject to clinging, and states that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging, are related to a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging by way of the condition of support (nissaya-paccaya):
one aggregate that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, together with the [heart-]base, is related to three aggregates by way of the condition of support; ...
pe ... two aggregates, together with the [heart-]base, are related to two aggregates [by way of the condition of support].
Condition by way of dependence.

Both states that are not-clung-to-but-susceptible-to-clinging and states that are neither-clung-to-nor-susceptible-to-clinging are conditions, by way of dependence, for a state that is not-clung-to-but-susceptible-to-clinging:
the aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-susceptible-to-clinging and the great primaries are conditions, by way of dependence, for mind-produced [matter].
Material phenomena are related to [other] material phenomena by way of the condition of support (nissaya-paccaya).

Both phenomena that are acquired and subject to clinging (upādinnupādāniya) and phenomena that are not acquired but subject to clinging (anupādinnupādāniya) are related to a phenomenon that is not acquired but subject to clinging by way of the condition of support:
the aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging, together with the primary elements (mahābhūta), are related to mind-produced [material phenomena].
It is a condition for material phenomena by way of the support-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*). One aggregate that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, together with the [heart-]base,
is a condition for three aggregates by way of the support-condition …pe… two aggregates, together with the base, are conditions for two aggregates by way of the support-condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging: as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakata-upanissaya*) ...
[etc] ... Natural decisive support: bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure; bodily pleasure for bodily pleasure ... [etc].
It is a condition for suffering by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). Bodily suffering is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily suffering, ...

[and so on] ... temperature is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily suffering, ... [and so on] ... food is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily suffering, ... [and so on] ... bodily pleasure, bodily suffering, temperature, and food.
Physical pleasure is related to physical pain by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of decisive support condition:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support ... [etc. ... Natural decisive support: having relied upon physical pleasure...

One gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha duty, arouses jhāna, arouses insight, arouses direct knowledge, arouses meditative attainment, kills a living being … [and so on] … causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Relying upon bodily pain … temperature … or food, one gives a gift … [and so on] … causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Bodily pain … [and so on] … [is a condition].
Pleasure … bodily pain … temperature … food is related to faith that is neither clung-to nor conducive to clinging, to virtue, to learning,
to generosity, to wisdom, to lust, to hatred, to delusion, to conceit, to wrong view, and to aspiration,
by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging.
As natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): relying on bodily pleasure, one arouses the Path and enters the attainment of fruition.
Relying on bodily pain... temperature... or food, one arouses the Path and enters the attainment of fruition.
Bodily pleasure … bodily pain … temperature … food is a condition for the path and for the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support …pe…. Natural decisive support: faith that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging …pe….

Depending upon [a state], one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance, arouses jhāna, arouses insight, arouses direct knowledge, arouses meditative attainment, conceives conceit, or adopts a wrong view.
[This includes] virtue that is not-clung-to but is subject to clinging; learning; generosity; wisdom; lust; hatred; and delusion.
… pride … view … aspiration … temperature … food … depending on a lodging,
one gives a gift … pe … arouses meditative attainment, conceives pride, adopts a [wrong] view, kills a living being … pe … causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Faith that is not acquired but subject to clinging … virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom … lust … hatred … [and so forth].

… delusion … conceit … view … aspiration … temperature … food … lodging … faith that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging … virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom … lust … hatred … delusion … conceit … view … aspiration is a condition for the first jhāna by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).

The preparation for the first jhāna is related to the first jhāna …pe… the preparation for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe… the first jhāna is related to the second jhāna …pe… the base of nothingness is related to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe… the taking of life is related to the taking of life …pe… fixed wrong view is related to fixed wrong view …pe….

A state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as above] … Natural decisive support:

relying on faith that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, one torments oneself and torments others, and experiences suffering rooted in searching. [Relying on] virtue that is not clung-to but subject to clinging … [and so forth].
... pe ... depending on a lodging, one torments oneself and afflicts oneself, experiencing suffering rooted in searching.
Faith that is not yet acquired but is subject to acquisition ... pe ...
is a condition for a lodging by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of decisive support-condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging—namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakata-upanissaya*) … [as above] … Natural decisive support:
the preliminary practice (*parikamma*) for the first path is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for the first path. [The preliminary practice for] the second path … [as above] …
The preparation for the third path … pe … the preparation for the fourth path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state that is not acquired through clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired through clinging and not subject to clinging by way of decisive support condition—
namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … pe … Natural decisive support— the first [path].
The path is a condition for the second path by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

The second path is [a condition] for the third path …pe… the third path is [a condition] for the fourth path …pe… the path is a condition for the attainment of fruition (*phala-samāpatti*) by way of the decisive support condition.

A state that is not acquired and not subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is acquired and subject to clinging by way of the decisive support condition—namely, as the proximate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*).
Natural strong-dependence condition … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: the attainment of fruition is a condition for bodily pleasure by way of strong-dependence condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not favorable to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired by clinging but favorable to clinging by way of strong-dependence condition—namely, object-strong-dependence and natural strong-dependence … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: the Noble Ones, depending on the Path … [as above] … by way of strong-dependence condition.
They arouse an unarisen attainment, they enter an arisen attainment, and they practice insight into formations as impermanent,

suffering, and non-self. The Path is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for the Noble Ones’ analytical knowledge of meaning, analytical knowledge of phenomena, analytical knowledge of language, analytical knowledge of eloquence, and skill in discerning what is possible and impossible.

A pre-arisen state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of pre-arisen condition, for a state that is clung-to and subject to clinging: namely, objective pre-arising and physical-basis pre-arising.
Regarding objective pre-arising: trainees or worldlings [perceive] the eye as impermanent, as suffering...
They contemplate [them] as non-self, yet they relish them and take delight in them; with that as the object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises;
when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, the resultant arises with that as its object.
[One contemplates] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … forms acquired by clinging and favorable to clinging … odors … flavors … tangibles … the physical basis as impermanent.
They practice insight into [the aggregates] as suffering and as non-self, yet they relish them and take delight in them;
with that as an object, lust arises …pe… mental distress arises. When wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, their result arises by way of having that as its object.
The appropriated and subject-to-clinging visible-object base is [the object] of eye-consciousness …pe… the appropriated and subject-to-clinging odor-base is [the object] of nose-consciousness.
…the taste base … the tangible object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. As base-pre-nascence:

the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the [heart-]base is a condition for the aggregates that are acquired through clinging and are objects of clinging by way of pre-nascence condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state that is not acquired but is subject to clinging—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.

Regarding object-prenascence: when one contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, or when one relishes it and delights in it, lust arises with respect to it … [and so on] … or grief arises. The ear … [and so on].
...pe... one contemplates the physical basis (vatthu) as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes it and delights in it;
with that as an object, lust arises ...pe... grief arises. With the divine eye, they see form that is both clung-to and subject to clinging.
As a pre-arising condition: the physical basis is a pre-arising condition for the aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging.

A state that is acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging. As a base-prenascence: the [heart-]base is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for the aggregates that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging.
A state that is not acquired but subject to clinging is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging. As object-prenascence:
in regard to forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles that are not acquired but subject to clinging, [one contemplates them] as impermanent...
One contemplates [it] as suffering and as non-self, yet relishes it and delights in it; with that as the object, lust arises … and so on … grief arises.
With the divine eye, one sees form that is not clung to but is subject to clinging;
with the divine ear-element, one hears sound.
A state that is not clung to but is subject to clinging is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state that is both clung to and subject to clinging. As object-prenascence:

one contemplates forms, sounds, odors, tastes, or tangibles that are not clung to but are subject to clinging as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes them and delights in them; taking them as object, lust arises... [and so on].
Mental distress arises. When wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, their result arises as an object-condition (*tadārammaṇatā*).
A form-base that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is a pre-arising condition for eye-consciousness; ... [and so on] ... a tangible-base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness.
Both states that are clung-to and subject to clinging, and states that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging, are pre-arising conditions for a state that is clung-to and subject to clinging.

Condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence. The non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging visible-object base and the eye base are related to eye-consciousness by way of prenascence condition …pe… the non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging tangible-object base and the body base are related to body-consciousness by way of prenascence condition. The non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging visible-object base and …pe… [and so on for the other sense bases].

The physical basis (*vatthu*) is a pre-arising condition for the aggregates that are both clung-to and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*) …pe… the tangible object base that is not clung-to but subject to clinging (*anupādinnupādāniya*) and the physical basis are pre-arising conditions for the aggregates that are both clung-to and subject to clinging.

Phenomena that are both clung-to and subject to clinging, as well as those that are not clung-to but subject to clinging, [are conditions] for a phenomenon that is not clung-to but subject to clinging.
Condition by way of prenascence condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence.

The non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging visible-object base and the [heart-]base are a condition by way of prenascence condition for the non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging aggregates …pe… the non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging tangible-object base and the [heart-]base are a condition by way of prenascence condition for the non-clung-to, subject-to-clinging aggregates.
Conditioned by prenascence condition.
A postnascent state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of postnascence condition— the postnascent...
Aggregates that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are related to this pre-arisen body that is clung-to and subject to clinging by way of post-nascence condition.
A state that is clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of post-nascence condition:
post-nascent aggregates that are clung-to and subject to clinging are related to this pre-arisen body that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of post-nascence condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging:

postnascence aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for this prenascent body which is both acquired and subject to clinging, and not acquired but subject to clinging.
A state that is not clung to but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not clung to but is subject to clinging by way of posteriority condition:
postnascence aggregates that are not clung to but are subject to clinging are a condition for this prenascent body that is not clung to but is subject to clinging by way of posteriority condition.
A state that is not clung to but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is clung to and is subject to clinging by way of posteriority condition: postnascence...
Aggregates that are not clung-to but are objects of clinging are a condition, by way of postnascence-condition, for this prenascent body which is both clung-to and an object of clinging.

A state that is not clung-to but is an object of clinging is a condition, by way of postnascence-condition, for a state that is both clung-to and an object of clinging, and for a state that is not clung-to but is an object of clinging— namely,
postnascent aggregates that are not clung-to but are objects of clinging [are conditions] for this prenascent...
A body that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and a body that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging, are related to [the mind] by way of postnascence condition.
A state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging is related to a state that is clung-to and subject to clinging by way of postnascence condition:
postnascent aggregates that are neither clung-to nor subject to clinging are related to this prenascent body that is clung-to and subject to clinging by way of postnascence condition.
A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging:

the posterior aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for this prior body that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging.

A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of posterior-arising condition, for a state that is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging and for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging:
postnascence aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are a condition,
by way of posterior-arising condition, for this prenascent body which is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging and neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging.
A state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is related to a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of the condition of repetition:
preceding aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging are related to succeeding aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging.

Conditioned by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*): adaptation (*anuloma*) is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*); adaptation is a condition for purification (*vodāna*) by way of repetition-condition.

A state that is not-clung-to but subject-to-clinging (*anupādinnupādāniya*) is a condition for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-subject-to-clinging (*anupādinnaanupādāniya*) by way of repetition-condition: change-of-lineage is a condition for the Path; purification is a condition for the Path by way of repetition-condition. Kamma...
A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging:

volition that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking, volition that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates and for the kamma-produced matter. Volition.

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of kamma-condition. A volition that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and for a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging... [by way of kamma-condition].
Condition by way of kamma-condition: volition that is acquired and subject to clinging is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not acquired but subject to clinging is a condition by way of kamma-condition for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging: [volition] that is not acquired but subject to clinging...
Volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the aggregates associated with it and for the material phenomena produced by consciousness.
A state that is not acquired through clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging:

asynchronous volition that is not acquired through clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition for resultant aggregates that are both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging, and for the material phenomena born of kamma-formations.
Condition by way of kamma-condition:
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging—whether co-nascent or asynchronous.
Co-nascent: volition that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.

Condition by way of kamma. Asynchronous: wholesome volition that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging.

A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging: volition that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not clung-to and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is both not clung-to and subject to clinging, and for a state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging: volition that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging is a condition,
by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A resultant state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging:
one resultant aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for three aggregates … [and so on] … two [aggregates].
Aggregates are related to two aggregates by way of resultant condition (*vipākapaccaya*).

At the moment of rebirth-linking, one resultant aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to three aggregates and to the kamma-produced matter (*kaṭattā-rūpa*) by way of resultant condition … pe … two aggregates are related to two aggregates and to the kamma-produced matter by way of resultant condition. Aggregates.

A state that is both acquired (*upādinnupādāniya*) and subject to clinging (*upādāniya*) is related to a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging by way of the condition of result (*vipākapaccaya*). A resultant state that is both acquired and subject to clinging—the aggregates that are resultant, acquired, and subject to clinging—is related to mind-produced matter by way of the condition of result.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is related to a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and to a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging... [by way of the condition of result].

Condition by way of resultant condition: one resultant aggregate that is both acquired through clinging and subject to clinging is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition …pe… two aggregates are conditions for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition.
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging by way of resultant condition:

one resultant aggregate that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for three aggregates by way of resultant condition … pe … two aggregates are conditions for two aggregates by way of resultant condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging: resultant aggregates that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of resultant condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state that is both not acquired by clinging but subject to clinging and not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging:
one resultant aggregate that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging [is a condition] for three...
The aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition …pe… two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition.
Nutriment.
A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of nutriment-condition (*āhāra-paccaya*).

Nutriments that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are a condition for associated aggregates by way of nutriment-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, nutriments that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are a condition for associated aggregates and for the types of form produced by karma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*) by way of nutriment-condition. [The state] that is both clung-to and subject to clinging...
Edible food is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for the body that is clung-to and subject to clinging.
A state that is clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging:

nutriments that are clung-to and subject to clinging are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for mind-produced matter; edible food that is clung-to and subject to clinging... [is a condition for the body].
Nutriment is a condition for the body that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, by way of the nutriment-condition.

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and for a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging, by way of the nutriment-condition:
the nutriments that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

Material phenomena are a condition for material phenomena by way of nutriment-condition. Edible food that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for the body that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and for the body that is not clung-to but subject to clinging, by way of nutriment-condition.

A phenomenon that is not clung-to but subject to clinging is a condition for a phenomenon that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of nutriment-condition—namely, [nutriment that is] not clung-to but subject to clinging...
Nutriments are related to the associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of nutriment condition.
Edible food that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is related to the body that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of nutriment condition.

A state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is related to a state that is clung-to and subject to clinging by way of nutriment condition—edible food that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is related to the body that is clung-to and subject to clinging by way of nutriment condition.
A state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging,
and for a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging: edible food that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is a condition,
by way of nutriment-condition, for the body that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and for the body that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging: nutriments that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for the associated aggregates.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging: nutriments that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state that is both not acquired by clinging and subject to clinging, and for a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging: nutriments that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition,
by way of nutriment-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

States that are both acquired and subject to clinging, and states that are not acquired but subject to clinging, are conditions by way of nutriment-condition for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging:
edible food that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition by way of nutriment-condition for the body that is both acquired and subject to clinging.
States that are both acquired and subject to clinging, and states that are not acquired but subject to clinging,

are related to a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging by way of nutriment condition: edible food that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and edible food that is not acquired but subject to clinging,
are related to the body that is not acquired but subject to clinging by way of nutriment condition.
States that are both acquired and subject to clinging, and states that are not acquired but subject to clinging, are related to states that are both acquired and subject to clinging,

and states that are not acquired but subject to clinging, by way of nutriment condition. Edible food that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and edible food that is not acquired but subject to clinging,
is related to the body that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and the body that is not acquired but subject to clinging, by way of nutriment condition.
A faculty that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a phenomenon that is acquired and subject to clinging:

the faculties that are acquired and subject to clinging are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for the associated aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking, the [faculties] that are acquired and subject to clinging...
The faculties are related to their associated aggregates and to the matter produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa) by way of faculty condition.

The eye-faculty is related to eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the body-faculty is related to body-consciousness ... [and so on] ... The material life-faculty is related to the matter produced by kamma by way of faculty condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging by way of the faculty-condition: the faculties that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the faculty-condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging and for a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging by way of the faculty-condition:
the faculties that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Material phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of faculty condition.
A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is related to a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging by way of faculty condition:
faculties that are not acquired by clinging but are subject to clinging are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of faculty condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging: the faculties that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for the associated aggregates.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging: the faculties that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for the material phenomena produced by mind.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a state that is both not acquired by clinging and subject to clinging, and for a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging. The faculties that are neither acquired by clinging nor subject to clinging are a condition,
by way of faculty-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Jhāna as a state both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of jhāna-condition, for a state both clung-to and subject to clinging:

jhāna factors that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are a condition, by way of jhāna-condition, for the associated aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking, [jhāna factors] that are both clung-to and subject to clinging...
The factors of jhāna are related to their associated aggregates and to kamma-produced matter by way of the jhāna condition.

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of the jhāna condition: the factors of jhāna that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are related to mind-originated matter by way of the jhāna condition.

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to both a state that is clung-to and subject to clinging and a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging... [by way of the jhāna condition].
Condition by way of jhāna: jhāna factors that are acquired and subject to clinging are a condition by way of jhāna for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not acquired but subject to clinging is a condition by way of jhāna for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging: [jhāna factors] that are not acquired but subject to clinging...
The jhāna factors are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of the jhāna condition.

A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is related to a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging by way of the jhāna condition: the jhāna factors that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are related to their associated aggregates by way of the jhāna condition.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging: the jhāna-factors that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for both a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging and a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging:
the jhāna-factors that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging [are a condition] for their associated [states].
The aggregates are a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for mind-originated matter.
Path:

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of the path-condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging—namely, those states that are both acquired and subject to clinging.
The path factors are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of path-condition (*maggapaccaya*). At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging by way of path-condition: the path factors that are both clung-to and subject to clinging are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of path-condition.

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and for a state that is not clung-to but subject to clinging ... [etc. ... by way of path-condition.
Condition by way of path: the path factors that are acquired and subject to clinging are a condition by way of path for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter.

A state that is not acquired but subject to clinging is a condition by way of path for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging: the [path factors] that are not acquired but subject to clinging...
The path factors are a condition, by way of path-condition, for the associated aggregates and for the mind-originated material phenomena.

A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of path-condition, for a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging: the path factors that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are a condition, by way of path-condition, for the associated aggregates.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of path-condition, for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging: the path-factors that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging are a condition, by way of path-condition, for mind-produced matter.

A state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of path-condition, for both a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging and a state that is not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging:
the path-factors that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging [are conditions] for their associated [states].
The aggregates are a condition, by way of path-condition, for mind-originated matter.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of association-condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging— [namely,] a state that is acquired and subject to clinging...
One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of association-condition … pe … two aggregates [are conditions] for two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….

A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging by way of association-condition— a state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging … pe … .

One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of association-condition … two aggregates [are conditions] for two aggregates … Non-clung-to and not subject to clinging state is a condition for non-clung-to and not subject to clinging state by way of association-condition:
one non-clung-to and not subject to clinging aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of association-condition.
Condition …pe… two aggregates are related to two aggregates …pe….
Dissociation:
A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is related to a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition—conascent.

Pre-arisen and post-arisen. Co-arisen: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for the types of matter produced by kamma (*kaṭattārūpa*) by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayuttapaccaya*).
The aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of dissociation-condition; the physical base is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation-condition.
Pre-arisen: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness...
It is a condition by way of dissociation-condition …pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of dissociation-condition.
The physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for the aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition.
Postnascent aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for this prenascent body that is acquired and subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition.
A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not acquired but is subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*):

namely, conascence, prenascence, and postnascence. As conascence: the aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of dissociation-condition. As prenascence: the physical basis (*vatthu*) is a condition for the aggregates that are not acquired but are subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition.
Condition: Postnascent aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging are related to this prenascent body that is not acquired but is subject to clinging by way of dissociation condition.

A state that is acquired and subject to clinging is related to a state that is not acquired and not subject to clinging by way of dissociation condition. Prenascent: The physical basis (vatthu) is related to the aggregates that are not acquired and not subject to clinging by way of dissociation condition.

A state that is both acquired and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and for a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging. Subsequently arisen aggregates that are both acquired and subject to clinging are a condition,
by way of dissociation-condition, for this previously arisen body which is both acquired and subject to clinging, and for [the mind] which is not acquired but subject to clinging.
A state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*):
namely, co-nascence and post-nascence. Co-nascent aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of dissociation-condition.
Post-nascent aggregates that are not clung-to but are subject to clinging are a condition for this pre-nascent [body] that is not clung-to but is subject to clinging...
A state that is not acquired by clinging but is subject to clinging is related to a state that is both acquired by clinging and subject to clinging by way of dissociation condition.

Subsequently arisen aggregates that are not acquired by clinging but are subject to clinging are related to this previously arisen body that is both acquired by clinging and subject to clinging by way of dissociation condition.
A condition by way of dissociation condition (*vippayuttapaccaya*).

A state that is not-clung-to-but-subservient-to-clinging (*anupādinnupādāniya*) is a condition by way of dissociation condition for a state that is both clung-to-and-subservient-to-clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*) and for a state that is not-clung-to-but-subservient-to-clinging. Subsequently arisen aggregates that are not-clung-to-but-subservient-to-clinging [are conditions] for this previously arisen...
A body that is both acquired and subject to clinging, and a body that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, are related to [the mind] by way of dissociation-condition.
A state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging is related to a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition.

Subsequently arisen aggregates that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging are related to this previously arisen body that is both acquired and subject to clinging by way of dissociation-condition.
Conditioned by dissociation condition.
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state that is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging:
[namely] conascence and postnascence. Conascent aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are [conditions] for mind-produced [matter].

[Material] form is a condition for [mental] states by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*). Postnascent aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are a condition for this prenascent body which is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging by way of dissociation-condition.
A state that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging and for a state that is not-clung-to-but-liable-to-clinging.

It is a condition by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*). Postnascent aggregates that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are a condition by way of dissociation-condition for this prenascent body that is both-clung-to-and-liable-to-clinging, as well as for the body that is neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging.
There is.
A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*):
namely, conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. As conascent:

one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition for three aggregates by way of presence-condition …pe… two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of presence-condition.

Condition: At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate that is both clung-to and subject to clinging is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates and for the types of matter produced by kamma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*) …pe… two aggregates are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for two aggregates and for the types of matter produced by kamma.
Aggregates [are a condition] for the physical base …pe… the physical base [is a condition] for the aggregates …pe… one [aggregate] … [and so on].
A great primary element … [as above] … the great primary elements are related to derived matter produced by kamma as a presence condition.
For non-percipient beings, one great primary element … [as above] … the great primary elements are related to derived matter produced by kamma as a presence condition.
Pre-arisen: Learners or worldlings practice insight into the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
They relish them and delight in them; with that as object, lust arises …pe… grief arises. When wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, their result arises as an object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*).

They practice insight into the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … into forms, odors, tastes, and tangibles that are acquired through clinging and subject to clinging … into the physical basis (*vatthu*) as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
They relish them and delight in them; with that as their object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises.
When wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, the resultant arises with that as its object.

A form base that is acquired and subject to clinging is the object of eye-consciousness … [and so on] … a smell base that is acquired and subject to clinging … a taste base … a tangible base that is acquired and subject to clinging is the object of body-consciousness.

... pe ... the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... pe ... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness ... pe ... the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition by way of presence-condition (atthipaccaya) for the aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging.
Subsequently arisen aggregates that are acquired and subject to clinging are a condition for this previously arisen body that is acquired and subject to clinging.

Condition by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*). Edible food that is acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*) is a condition by way of presence condition for the body that is acquired and subject to clinging.
